column3: The Hebrew says the Philistine rulers passed in hundreds and thousands; BSB explicitly makes them marching out “their units.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the Philistine commanders as the recipients of Achish’s reply and joins days and years with “or.” BSB leaves the addressees implicit and uses “days, even years.”
The Hebrew twice names “the commanders of the Philistines” and says the man may win favor by “the heads of those men.” BSB names the commanders once and renders the heads as those “of our men.”
The Hebrew says his going out and coming in are good “in my eyes”; BSB attaches “in my sight” to his uprightness and says the marching “seems right.”
The Hebrew says not to do evil “in the eyes of the Philistine rulers”; BSB renders this as doing nothing to displease them.
The Hebrew describes David’s service as being “before you”; BSB renders this as having come to Achish.
The Hebrew explicitly says the commanders prohibited going “up” with them into battle; BSB leaves the upward direction implicit.
The Hebrew repeats rising early in the morning, shifting from singular to plural address; BSB combines this into one instruction to rise early.
